fields_method: The six member subobjects come from ctor/dtor call displacements in the ROM. Everything at 0x428 and above comes from decoding all 0x1684 bytes of the class's .text and collecting every LDR/STR immediate displacement in 0x420..0x47b. Offsets 0x45e-0x45f, 0x46a-0x46b and 0x479-0x47b never appear at any width and are padding; every other 4-byte slot from 0x428 to 0x478 is touched. This reproduces include/PiranhaPlant.h's map exactly, so the header's OFFSETS are ROM-confirmed. The NAMES are not -- see unproven.

divergences_to_consider: The header declares `virtual ~PiranhaPlant();` as the FIRST virtual, out of line. Both promoted dEnemyBase_c oracles took the opposite shape: daOts_c.h and daObjMarioCap_c.h define the destructor INLINE in the class body so that a later out-of-line virtual becomes the key function. Which shape this class takes decides whether the TU emits the _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS group, and that group's canonical copy is in ov084 .data, which no shard owns. This is a stage-2 codegen decision; it is recorded here because the ROM does not settle it.

InitResources, CleanupResources, Behavior, Render and OnPendingDestroy are declared WITHOUT the `virtual` keyword. This is not a defect: they redeclare virtuals fBase_c.h already declares (slots 0/3/6/9/12) and `typedef signed int s32` in include/types.h makes the header's `int` return types identical to fBase_c's `s32`, so they override correctly. It is only inconsistent with include/BobOmbBuddy.h, which spells the same five `virtual s32`.
The header does not mention the 9-entry state PMF array or any of the 15 non-virtual functions.

blockers.what: The .init/.ctor boundary does not separate daFPkn_c from daPkn_c.
blockers.detail: ov084 has 3 sinit functions and 3 .ctor entries for 4 classes. __sinit_ov084_0213035c is daKrb_c's alone and __sinit_ov084_02130558 is daRedBombhei_c's alone, but __sinit_ov084_02130654 builds daPkn_c's 9 PMF records AND constructs .bss objects that only the daFPkn_c run reads (0x02130e04, 0x02130e1c). Together with the shared .rodata pointer table at 0x021302f4 and four shared .bss objects, that is evidence the two classes were ONE original translation unit. It does not block a text-only promotion of the daPkn_c run -- the sinit shards stay separate .c files -- but it means the queue's two rows may not correspond to two original .cpp files. tools/tu_map.py disagrees and puts a boundary between them; use decomp-tu-slicing before assuming either.
